chapter: Las Vegas, Sinatra and later years
title: The Sands lounge quintet; commuting home
summary: Sinatra's invitation leads to a long run at the Sands with Jerry Dodgion, and Norvo flew home weekly to Eve.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: So I said, Pete would be great for it, so I wrote -- so we did it, so he was pleased and then he said what're you doing about Vegas, this year? I said, Gee, I don't know, I was supposed to go back in for Monte. He said, Well, I'm going in the Sands beginning in February, said call Monte.

So I called Monte, I said, 'You made any plans for me?' He said, 'See Red, I forgot, I haven't done it at all,' I said, 'Well, I got a chance to go another place,' I said for a month or two. He said, 'Go ahead.' So I said to Frank, 'I hate to do it with a trio, it's too hard in the lounges,' so he said, 'All right, add a couple of men.' So, I called Gene Wright, I said, 'Do you know anybody that's a cookin' anyplace I could (unintelligible) little saxophone player that plays good? He said, 'Yeah, I know, Jerry Dodgion,' so I got him and drummer and we opened in the Sands.
Now we opened there in February in the Lounge. He was -- Frank was in the big room. So, we stayed there until Labor Day.
No kidding?
All summer. And the quintet, had five of us started starring. That's where we started. At the --
And that was a good gig, it wasn't --
Yeah, and then we got a drummer from San Francisco, name of John Markham. And he was great --
Was Eve able to join you there?
Oh, we lived up there during the summer.
OH, yeah.
But see, in those days I used to come home every weekend, a plane was very cheap then.
Yeah.
I could fly to Los Angeles and back, I
could leave at 4:00 in themorning, Sunday morning and be there in an hour and 20 minutes .
Yeah .

Eve would pick me up and I'd have all day Sunday, and Monday I'd leave at 9:00 o'clock and they moved my schedule back so that I'd get there at 10:00 or so and I could make the 11:00 o'clock starting date .
Yeah .
So it was like two days a week home.
Sure.
Then when school was out, they all came up.
Yeah.
And they spent the summer there .
Yeah, that was very good.
So it was kind of -- we did that for summers after summer.
AT the Sands, everytime.
Yeah, for years . I worked the Sands for 15 years, probably more.
Really?
